identification.name: Inconel 625 (Annealed)
identification.common_form_notes: Available as sheet (ASTM B443), plate (B443), bar/rod (B446), tube (B444), and welded pipe (B705) from aerospace and corrosion-resistant alloy suppliers. Supplied as gas-atomised powder (15–45 µm) for metal AM. Also used as weld filler wire (ERNiCrMo-3, AWS A5.14). UNS N06625, Werkstoff Nr. 2.4668, DIN NiCr22Mo9Nb.
identification.notes: Inconel 625 is a solid-solution-strengthened nickel–chromium–molybdenum–niobium superalloy (UNS N06625). Properties are for the annealed condition (980–1150°C, air cool) per ASTM B443/B446. Unlike Inconel 718, no precipitation hardening is required — Mo (8–10%) and Nb (3.2–4.2%) in solid solution provide strength up to ~982°C without a complex ageing cycle. Exceptional corrosion resistance: superior pitting, crevice, and intergranular corrosion resistance in seawater and aggressive chloride environments; resists both oxidising and reducing acids. Max continuous service temperature ~982°C (short-term oxidation resistance to 1093°C; mechanical strength is limiting above ~982°C). Cryogenic toughness is excellent — Charpy impact energy 47–66 J at −196°C, suitable for cryogenic tankage and LNG service. Weldability is outstanding: no post-weld heat treatment is required to maintain corrosion resistance (not susceptible to sensitisation), and 625 is widely used as weld overlay and cladding (filler wire ERNiCrMo-3). In metal AM (DMLS/SLM/LPBF), 625 is one of the most printable superalloys — it does not suffer the hot cracking from γ″ precipitation that challenges Inconel 718 during AM. As-built SLM parts exhibit columnar dendritic microstructure with significantly higher strength (UTS up to ~1,240 MPa) but reduced ductility compared with wrought annealed; solution anneal and HIP restore ductility and eliminate porosity. Hardness HV 200 is approximate, converted from 190 HB. Shear strength derived from von Mises criterion: UTS/√3 = 930/√3 ≈ 537 MPa. Electrical conductivity derived from resistivity 1.29 µΩ·m: (0.01724/1.29) × 100 ≈ 1.3% IACS. Thermal diffusivity derived from k, ρ, Cp.

typical_usage: Seawater and offshore hardware (risers, subsea valves, umbilicals); chemical process vessels and piping; flue gas desulphurisation systems; aerospace engine components (combustor liners, exhaust systems) above 700°C; cryogenic tankage and LNG equipment; nuclear waste containment; weld cladding and hardfacing on lower-alloy substrates.
